project: ไร่สุขใจ (Rai Sukjai): a Thai-countryside farming game
about: Central asset list. The mechanics agent (Claude Code) writes each asset's spec and prompt. The asset agent reads it, creates the file at `output` and stamps the status fields back here. Full rules: assets/README.md.

statuses.in_progress: claimed by an asset agent (set `agent` and `updated_at`)
statuses.done: file created at `output`; `file` set to that path; waiting for review
statuses.needs_changes: reviewer wrote what to fix in `review`; asset agent redoes it and sets done again. The game keeps using the existing `file` until then.
statuses.approved: accepted; the game may use it
statuses.blocked: cannot be done as specified; explain in `notes`

protocol.everything_else: owned by the mechanics agent; do not change it. Leave suggestions in `notes`.
protocol.paint: Each asset's `paint` block has its own status flow (same statuses as above). The asset agent may edit paint.status, paint.file, paint.agent, paint.updated_at and paint.notes; the reviewer paint.status and paint.review; everything else in the block belongs to the mechanics agent. The game draws paint.file when paint.status is done or approved, otherwise the old `file`.

style_guide.look: Warm, hand-drawn cartoon in the style of 2000s Flash games: thick dark-brown outlines (#3a2213) about 2–3 px at 1× with round joins and caps, flat colour fills, at most one simple highlight or shade shape per part, slightly chunky and friendly proportions. No gradients (except the sky in backgrounds), no photorealism, no soft airbrush shading, no drop shadows (the game adds shadows).
style_guide.setting: Central Thai countryside (rice paddies, sugar palms, wooden stilt houses, village market). Culturally accurate and respectful details.
style_guide.originality: Original art only. Do NOT copy or trace the original 'The Farmer' / 'Sim Farm' Flash game graphics or any other existing game.
style_guide.text: No text inside images unless the prompt asks for it. The game renders all labels itself.
file_rules: SVG preferred: viewBox="0 0 W H" matching `canvas`, and width/height attributes equal to the canvas.
Transparent background for everything except `background` assets.
Self-contained: no external links, fonts, scripts or embedded raster images. Convert text to paths.
Prefix any id attributes with the asset id with dots replaced by '-' (e.g. crop-phrik-s3-leaf) so files can be inlined together.
Keep each file under 40 KB; backgrounds under 200 KB.
If SVG is impossible, a PNG at 2× the canvas size is accepted: save it next to `output` with a .png extension and put that path in `file`.
style_guide.anchor: `anchor` is the [x, y] point in canvas pixels that the game places on the target spot. For crops it is the soil point the plant grows from. For characters, animals and props it is where the feet or base touch the ground. For icons it is the centre.
style_guide.consistency: Keep the same outline weight, palette and lighting (light from top-left) across all assets. The five stages of one crop must clearly be the same plant growing.
style_guide.isometric: The farm scene is ISOMETRIC (2:1 dimetric): grid point (gx, gy) at height z maps to screen x = 290 + (gx - gy)·32, y = 226 + (gx + gy)·16 - z. Ground-plane directions: +gx runs down-right (32, 16) per tile, +gy runs down-left (-32, 16). Vertical edges stay vertical. The village map and the duck pen are isometric too, each on its own grid: village x = 400 + (u - v)·32, y = 70 + (u + v)·16 - z; pen x = 520 + (u - v)·32, y = 200 + (u + v)·16 - z. The market stall interior is FRONT VIEW, like a stage set. Characters and the pen props stay upright sprites.
style_guide.stage: The game stage is 600 px high and as wide as the screen allows, from 800 (4:3, iPad) to 1400 (21:9, tall phones); wider screens get side bars. The centred 800x600 area is the SAFE AREA: everything interactive stays inside it and all scene coordinates in prompts are safe-area coordinates (x 0–800). Full-stage backgrounds are painted with BLEED: 300 px of extra scenery on each side (canvas 1400x600, anchor (300, 0)), continuing the scene naturally and never holding anything the player must see or tap. An 800-wide background is still accepted: the game mirrors it into the margins.
style_guide.scale: Farm objects: scenery (house, trees, palms, bananas, huts, forest) is about 20 px per metre: the Thai house's stilts are ~2.2 m (44 px), bananas 3–4 m, palms 5–10 m, forest trees 10–25 m. The farmer, dragon jar and buffalo are the farm's characters and get a stylised game size of about 2x life (farmer ~67 px tall, jar ~55 px, buffalo ~75 px long, spirit house ~110 px tall); the ox cart stays near life size. Assets may be drawn larger; the game scales them (FARM_SCALE, and the scale in BANANA_SPOTS / PALM_SPOTS in js/art/iso.js). Crops and signs with text keep their gameplay sizes.

categories.crop: Plant at a growth stage, drawn over a soil tile. Canvas 64×64, anchor (32,56). Keep the plant inside x 6–58 and y 4–60 so neighbouring plots overlap only slightly.
categories.crop_overlay: Transparent layer placed on top of a crop.
categories.produce_icon: Harvested item, 32×32, centred. Reused at 18–40 px.
categories.hud_icon: Small HUD icon, 24×24, must read at 17 px.
categories.tile: Isometric soil block for one farm plot: 2:1 diamond top face (56×28) plus a 7 px deep block. Canvas 64×40, anchor (32,16) = centre of the top face. 48 of them sit in 4 fields of 4×3.
categories.tile_overlay: Transparent layer placed on top of an isometric soil tile (same canvas and anchor).
categories.character: People. Anchor = between the feet (or the waist for Auntie Daeng).
categories.animal: Animals. Anchor = ground under the body.
categories.prop: Interactive or foreground objects. Anchor = base on the ground.
categories.scenery: Decorative background pieces, some animated. Variants of the same thing share a `variant_group` (e.g. banana_clump) and the same canvas and anchor so they are interchangeable.
categories.background: Full stage: an 800×600 safe area, plus 300 px of bleed on each side when the canvas is 1400×600 (see style_guide.stage). Respect the KEEP CLEAR zones in the prompt.
categories.kit: Scene kit piece: one object the game places on a scene's grid to assemble the scene (reused across scenes). Painted PNG at `scale`, transparent, anchor = the ground point under the object, `footprint` = its size on the ground in tiles [down-right, down-left]. Delivered with a normal map at `normal`.
categories.ground: Painted ground layer of an assembled scene: everything flat (grass, floors, paths, water) plus the far backdrop, and nothing else that stands up.

paint_style.about: ART STYLE v3 (flat, hand-made look). Scenes are assembled from kit pieces that all share ONE outline, ONE palette, ONE cel-shading rule, ONE isometric camera and ONE size chart, so every piece lines up with every other. The earlier soft painterly pass read as AI-generated; v3 replaces it for kit pieces (see docs/map-design-guide.md, section 2.3).
paint_style.target: assets/painted/_style/target.jpg is the look to match (colour, light, softness, line weight, cuteness). Use it as the style reference image (Midjourney --sref, an IP-Adapter / style-reference input, or attach it and say 'match this art style').
paint_style.look: Clean 2D game-asset art: bold closed outline around every piece, flat colour fills, simple 3-tone cel shading (light side / base / shadow side) with hard edges between tones, a few inner lines for folds, planks, leaf clumps and roof rows. Shapes are simple, chunky and readable; details are grouped (leaves in 5–9 clumps, not hundreds of leaves; 4–6 planks, not 20). No gradients, no airbrush, no brush or noise texture, no glow, no blur.
paint_style.light: One sun from the upper-left for every piece: the light tone on surfaces facing up/left, the shadow tone on surfaces facing down/right, one small hard highlight on glossy things (eggs, glaze, water). No cast shadow on the ground (the game draws it). Moving light comes later from the normal map.
paint_style.view: Isometric game camera: 2:1 dimetric, looking down about 30°. Ground-plane edges run along the diagonals (down-right and down-left at 26.6°); vertical edges stay vertical. Characters, crops, trees and icons are upright sprites seen from that camera (3/4 view from slightly above). The asset's layout image shows the exact angle.
paint_style.characters: Chibi proportions: head about 40% of the body height, big glossy eyes with two highlights, soft blush, small rounded hands and feet, friendly expressions. Thai countryside people, dressed as each prompt says; culturally accurate and respectful (งอบ straw hats, ผ้าขาวม้า checked cloth, ม่อฮ่อม indigo shirts). Keep each character identical across its variants (same face, outfit, colours).
paint_style.setting: Central Thai countryside: rice paddies, sugar and coconut palms, banana clumps, teak stilt houses, spirit houses, village markets. Original art only: do not copy existing games.
paint_style.prompt_suffix: flat 2D game asset, bold clean dark brown outline, flat colours, three-tone cel shading with hard edges, simple chunky shapes, limited palette, isometric 3/4 view, vector illustration, crisp edges, transparent background
paint_style.negative_prompt: painterly, brush strokes, soft shading, airbrush, gradient, noise, grain, texture overlay, photorealistic, 3d render, glow, bloom, blur, depth of field, lens effects, tiny details, cluttered, cast shadow, text, watermark, frame, background

files.sprites: PNG, RGBA with a clean transparent background (no halo, no leftover white fringe, no drop shadow unless the prompt asks). Exact pixel size = paint.size (the asset's canvas × paint.scale).
files.backgrounds: WebP (quality about 0.85), opaque, exact pixel size = paint.size (1400×600 canvas × 2). The centred 1600×1200 px area is the safe area; the 600 px strips on each side are bleed that continues the scene.
files.size_budget: Aim for sprites under 300 KB and backgrounds under 1.5 MB (tools/check-assets.mjs warns above that).

paint_style.placement: paint.layout is a render of the current art at exactly paint.size. The painted subject must occupy the same place: same footprint, same base point, same height and pose. The anchor is at pixel (anchor × paint.scale); for most sprites that is the ground point under the object. Keep the whole subject inside the canvas and do not crop or pad the canvas. For overlays (bugs, fertilizer, egg piles) keep the exact positions shown.
workflow: 1. Read paint_style, then work through the queue with `node tools/check-assets.mjs --paint` (lowest paint.batch first, then priority).

2. Batch 0 is the STYLE ANCHOR set (farmer, duck, egg basket, trough, soil tile, ripe chili, duck pen background). Paint it first and stop for review: everything else follows whatever gets approved there.

3. For each asset: stamp paint.status 'in_progress' with paint.agent and paint.updated_at. Generate from paint.prompt + prompt_suffix, with negative_prompt, using target.jpg as the style reference and paint.layout as the composition input (img2img at denoise 0.55–0.75, or ControlNet lineart / depth / tile). Generate large, then downscale to paint.size and align the subject to the layout image.
4. Keep variants consistent: paint a crop's five stages, the ten egg piles, the five banana clumps, the palms and each character's variants in one session with the same seed and settings.
5. Remove the background cleanly for sprites, save to paint.output, stamp paint.status 'done', paint.file = paint.output and paint.updated_at. Put anything the reviewer should know in paint.notes.
6. Run `node tools/check-assets.mjs`: it must print OK (it checks the file exists, its pixel size and, for sprites, the alpha channel).
paint_style.text: No text inside any image except the logo (ไร่สุขใจ / RAI SUKJAI). The game renders all labels and signs itself.

normal_maps.what: For every asset with a `normal` field, also deliver a tangent-space normal map: same pixel size and silhouette (same alpha) as the colour PNG, saved at `normal`. The game will use it to light the piece from a moving sun and lanterns.
normal_maps.convention: OpenGL style: red = surface facing right (+X), green = facing UP the image (+Y), blue = facing the viewer. A flat surface facing the viewer is (128, 128, 255). Keep it smooth and rounded like the painted forms: rounded canopy blobs, cylindrical bamboo and posts, planar roof and wall planes following the isometric faces.
normal_maps.how: Generate from the finished colour sprite with a normal-map tool (Laigter, SpriteIlluminator, Sprite DLight) or a depth model (Depth Anything / Marigold) converted to normals, then clean up by hand so the big planes read correctly.
normal_maps.light_in_colour: Because the game adds the strong light, paint kit pieces with SOFT built-in light: the same upper-left sun but gentle shading, no dark cast shadows and no shadow on the ground, only a faint darkening where the object touches the ground.

paint_style.kits: Scenes are being rebuilt from kits (duck pen first): a painted ground layer plus separate pieces the game places and depth-sorts. See assets/painted/_layout/pen_kit_composition.jpg for where every piece of the pen goes, and each piece's `layout` guide for its canvas, anchor, footprint and height.

stroke.outline: #3a2213, about 2.5 px wide at the asset's canvas size (canvas units, not file pixels), round joins and caps, around the whole silhouette and between big parts (roof vs wall, trunk vs crown).
stroke.inner: #6b4428 at about 1.2 px for interior detail lines (planks, leaf veins, straw strands, rope).
stroke.rule: Same widths on every piece, so a fence post and the duck house have the same line weight in the game.

paint_style.palette_rule: Kit SVG fills use ONLY these hex values (each material: [light, base, shadow]); outlines use line.outline / line.inner. tools/check-assets.mjs rejects other colours, gradients, filters, patterns and embedded images in kit SVGs.
consistency: Camera: the game's 2:1 isometric view; ground edges on the 26.6° diagonals, verticals vertical. Build each piece on the iso grid shown in its guide.
Scale: canvas units are game pixels. Match `height_px` and `footprint`; the farmer is about 67 px tall (see docs/map-design-guide.md, section 2.3).
Anchor: the ground point under the piece sits exactly on the guide's anchor cross.
Same outline widths, same palette tones, same light direction on every piece.

Check assets/painted/_layout/kit_board.png (node tools/kit-board.mjs): every piece at game size on one grid next to the farmer. Anything that looks heavier, brighter, bigger or differently lit than its neighbours is wrong.
workflow_v3: Read docs/style-contract.md and assets/painted/_style/generation_profile.json (fill the profile before the first batch; keep it fixed across batches).
Build every prompt from paint_style.prompt_template: style references = locked anchors; geometry reference = the layout guide.
Generate, then finish: trace, snap fills to the right material's palette tones, clean islands and jagged contours, redraw the outline as strokes at the locked widths.
Commit the approved pre-trace image as assets/painted/_source/<id>.png (canvas × 2).

Validate: node tools/check-assets.mjs (palette, format, normal map) and node tools/validate-kit.mjs (anchor, height, outline, footprint, silhouette and detail kept versus the source, detail versus the anchors).
Compare the batch at actual game size on the kit board: node tools/kit-board.mjs. Fix anything that stands out before stamping done.
Normal map: render the final SVG at 2× and save to `normal` with the recorded Laigter settings.

style_anchors.rule: Style anchors are the owner-approved finished kit pieces that define v3 for every later batch: the artwork from commit 7a553f8. `node tools/lock-style-anchors.mjs` renders them to assets/painted/_style/anchors/ and records their sha256; tests fail if a locked anchor changes. Their @4x renders are the STYLE reference in every prompt; layout guides are the GEOMETRY reference only.
style_anchors.reference_board: The owner's Night Camp asset board (supplied out of band) sets the target craftsmanship: natural silhouettes, layered botanical foliage, sculpted forms, convincing construction, readable material detail. It is a quality target only; never trace or copy it.

prompt_template.rule: Every generation prompt has these four labelled parts, in this order. Never mix their roles.
prompt_template.1_style_references: STYLE (controls look only): the locked anchor renders assets/painted/_style/anchors/kit.duck_house@4x.png, kit.tree_round_a@4x.png and kit.fence_span_se@4x.png, plus docs/style-contract.md. Match their silhouette quality, material detail, palette use, line weight and upper-left light.
prompt_template.2_geometry_reference: GEOMETRY (controls placement only): the entry's `layout` guide: canvas, anchor cross, footprint diamond, height line. It has no style; do not copy its colours or flat shapes.
prompt_template.3_subject: SUBJECT: the entry's `prompt` (what the object is).
prompt_template.4_settings: SETTINGS: paint_style.prompt_suffix and negative_prompt, plus the fixed values in assets/painted/_style/generation_profile.json.

size_chart.about: In-game size of characters, animals and props in the iso scenes, so they share one scale with the kit (kit pieces are drawn at game size). The game scales each asset's canvas to this size (SIZE_CHART / gameScale in js/art/assets.js). New art for these ids should be drawn at this size (canvas units = game px).
size_chart.prop.nest: 100 px wide (egg piles share its scale)
size_chart.reference: duck house 105 px, round tree 140–170 px, fence post 36 px
